McKeown shows how people keep vague yeses in circulation because they fear awkwardness more than dilution, then answers with a harder rule: separate the decision from the relationship and build a repertoire of graceful refusals. The chapter matters because the chapter translates essential intent into a boundary the world can actually hear.
